name: How much does it cost to add glass office partitions versus drywall?

mainEntity.name: Is it worth using glass conference rooms and offices instead of traditional drywall partitions in an office build-out?
mainEntity.text: Is it worth using glass conference rooms and offices instead of traditional drywall partitions in an office build-out?

acceptedAnswer.text: Glass partitions are often chosen for premium office build-outs because they create an open, modern look and bring daylight deeper into the space. They can improve branding and make smaller offices feel larger. Drywall partitions, however, are usually less expensive and provide better sound control, so they may be the better choice for private offices, sensitive meetings, or budget-conscious projects. In Los Angeles-area office spaces, the decision often comes down to how the tenant balances image, privacy, and cost. Some projects use a hybrid approach, with glass in reception and conference rooms and drywall in support areas. That approach can deliver a high-end feel without turning the entire project into a premium-cost build-out. The right choice should be made early, because partition type affects electrical, HVAC, and fire-life-safety planning.
acceptedAnswer.description: Glass partitions usually cost more than drywall but can make a space feel brighter, more open, and more premium. Drywall is generally cheaper and better for privacy, sound control, and budget-focused layouts.
